exposure: prenatal appearance of the foramen ovale
Infants who did not undergo Rashkind procedure before cardiac surgery
maximum velocity of flow through the foramen ovale
Infants who underwent Rashkind procedure within 24 hours of birth
fetal cardiac size (heart area/chest area ratio)
rate of disproportion between left and right ventricle
outcome: Need for Rashkind procedure within 24 hours of birth
cohort: 98 fetuses diagnosed prenatally with dextro-transposition of the great arteries at two European centers between 2006 and 2013
finding: In fetuses with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, increased pulmonary venous blood flow and a flattened foramen ovale valve on prenatal ultrasound were associated with the need for a Rashkind procedure within 24 hours of birth.
mod_finding: The study found no difference in the rate of Cesarean delivery between two groups of fetuses with d-TGA (those who underwent a Rashkind procedure within 24 hours of birth and those who did not).
